column2: Flow as a bull with the stream, joyful for the Maruts too, bearing all with strength.
You, the upholder, flowing, seer of heaven, I urge on in battles, the strong one.
With this thought, bay one, flow with the drinking stream; urge on your fellow in battles.
The red bull, roaring toward the cows, you go sounding through earth and heaven; like Indra's call heard in the contest, you send forth this word.
Swelling with milk, delightful, you go, stirring the honeyed stalk; flowing, you go making continuity, sprinkled around for Indra, Soma.
So flow, joyful, for exhilaration, bowing the slayer of the one with raised grasp; bearing a shining hue, desiring cattle, flow around us, sprinkled, Soma.
We singers call on you alone in the winning of strength; you, Indra, lord of the good among Vritras; men call on you, as racers at the goals.
You, wondrous, thunderbolt-handed, great, praised, O stone-bearer — scatter for us cows, horses and chariots, Indra, as strength to a winner.
He goes boldly forth like a hundred-fold host; he slays Vritras for the giver; his streams swell like those of a mountain, the gifts of the much-nourishing.
Rejoice, O fair-jawed, bay-horsed one; we ask of you; through you the ordainers are adorned; your praiseworthy glories are comparable, O lover of songs, at the pressings, Indra.
Slayer of the hostile Vritra, winner of strength day by day, you are the giver of cattle and horses.
Be mixed, red one, like cows with good udders; settling like a falcon into its nest.
The cows, the bold ones, have sung together for exhilaration; the flowing drops of soma make paths.
Bring, flowing one, the most vigorous, famed wealth, which overcomes the five peoples, by which we may win.
The ancient seer flows with the wise, held by men, and has run round the vessels; creating the name of Trita, dripping honey, he increases Indra and Vayu for friendship.
This one, purifying, made the dawns shine; this one became a world-maker for the rivers; milking thrice seven mixtures, Soma flows, a lovely exhilaration for the heart.
So indeed you are hero-loving, so brave and steady; so your mind is to be won.
So is your gift, O much-bountiful, set by all supporters; then, Indra, be with us.
Do not, like the prayer, be Indra's own, O lord of strengths; rejoice in the pressed soma with cattle.
In your friendship, Indra, we strong ones fear not, lord of strength; we praise you, victorious and unconquered.
The many gifts of Indra, his helps, are not lost, when he bestows bounty of strength with cattle upon singers.
These drops have been released, swift, across the filter, to all good fortunes.
Driving away many evils, the strong give good paths for offspring, making the horses by themselves.
Making room for the cow, they flow toward fair praise, for us a regulated Ida.
The king goes with wisdom, flowing over Manu, to travel through the air.
O Soma, bring us strength, speedy, like a form for splendor; as you are pressed for the gods' feast.
Bring us, O drop, hundredfold cattle, nourishment with good horses; carry fortune for help.
With good deeds we praise you, bearing manly treasures in the seats of great heaven, lovely.
The hymn-worthy, bold-grasping, great of great vows, exhilaration, breaker of a hundred forts.
From you wealth has come to the king, O skilful, from heaven; the fair-winged unfaltering has brought it.
Then, urged on, he has gained greater power and greatness; the all-seeing fulfiller of wishes.
To the whole world, to see the light, the common, space-crossing guardian of truth bears.
Purifying, make room, O lover of songs, bring strength to the people, O bay one, as you are released with the milk-mixture.
Purifying, go to the gods' feast, to the appointed place of Indra, shining, set by the racers.
By Agni is Agni kindled, the seer, lord of the house, the youth, carrier of offering, whose mouth is the ladle.
O god Agni, the lord of offerings who honors you, the messenger — be his helper.
To him who, with offering, serves Agni for the gods' feast, be kind, O purifier.
I call Mitra of pure skill and Varuna the devourer of foes, who fulfill the ghee-dripping thought.
By truth, Mitra and Varuna, strengtheners of truth, touching truth, you attained great skill.
Mitra and Varuna, our seers, born in many, widely dwelling, give skillful work.
You are seen together with fearless Indra, joyful, with the same radiance.
Then, by their own way, they again took on the state of embryo, bearing a sacrificial name.
You found the cows firmly, even in the hidden place, with the carriers, Indra, with the strong.
I call on those two by whom all this was made of old; Indra and Agni are not harmed.
We call Indra and Agni, fierce, smiting the enemies; may they be gracious to us in such a case.
You slew the Aryan enemies, you slew the Dasa ones, lords of the good; you slew all hatreds.
The flowing king, the god, crosses the sea with a wave, the great truth; flow by the law of Mitra and Varuna, urging the great truth.
Held by men, desirable, all-seeing, king, god of the sea.
The cows and milch-cows long for Soma; the sages with thoughts ask for Soma; Soma, pressed, is praised, being purified; in Soma the hymns, the Trishtubhs, resound.
So, Soma, being sprinkled, flow to us purified, with well-being; enter Indra with great exhilaration; strengthen speech, beget plenty.
You, bull, have filled all with your manly greatness, O strongest; protect us, bounteous, in the cow-pen, thunderbolt-bearer, with wondrous helps.
The men sing to you at the pressing, O Vasu, in solitude, with hymns; when, thirsty, will you come to the pressed soma, to the house, Indra, like a bull to the cow.
With the Kanvas, bold one, you give boldly a thousandfold strength; O bounteous, all-seeing, tawny-formed, we swiftly ask for cattle-rich wealth.
Ill praise is not spoken among the givers of wealth; wealth does not reach the unyielding; good power, bounteous, belongs to you, to give to one like me, which is in the farther heaven.
The great mothers of truth have sung, adorning the child of heaven.
Four oceans of wealth for us from all sides, Soma; flow to us a thousandfold.
The pressed, most honeyed, exhilarating somas for Indra have flowed with the filter; may your exhilarations go to the gods.
The drop flows for Indra, said the gods; the lord of speech, master of the rite, ruler of all by might.
The thousand-streamed ocean flows, rousing speech; lord of Soma, of riches, friend of Indra day by day.
The filter of heat is spread in heaven's place; his threads worship and stand apart; the swift ones protect his purifier; they climb the back of heaven with fire.
The bounteous one clothes himself with heroic fame, kindled, shining, well offered; may his favor to us be ever greater; may he come with strengths.
By which you found lights for the Ayu and for Manu, rejoicing, you shine over his grass.
Today too the singers praise that of yours as before; win the bull-husbanded waters day by day.
Hear the call of him, Indra, who worships you crookedly; fill us with heroic wealth and cattle; you are great.
Indra, whoever has brought forth for you the newest, joyful song, a wise thought, swelling the ancient of truth.
We praise him whom songs and hymns have strengthened, Indra; desiring to win many of his boats, we seek.
O flowing one, your Ashvini cows, the divine, have been released with milk to the holder; from the air your steadfast ones have been released, who adorn you, O creators of sages.
On both sides the rays of the flowing, the banners of the firm one, go around; when the bay one is cleansed on the filter, he sits settled in the nest, in the vessels.
All abodes, all-seeing; the banners of you, the skilful lord, go around you; you pervade, flow, Soma, by law; you are lord of all the worlds and reign.
O flowing king, your essence is exhilarating, free from distress; it runs to the woolen sieve.
The essence of you, flowing one, shines skilful and radiant, light for the whole world to see.
We think of the well-gone bridge, hard to cross; may we overcome the lawless Dasyu.
The sound of the strong flowing one is heard like that of rain; lightnings move in the sky.
Flow to us great food, drop, with cattle and gold, with horses, Soma, with heroes.
Flow, all-seeing; fill the great heaven and earth, like Dawn, like the Sun with rays.
Flow around us on all sides with the sheltering stream, Soma, like a moving essence the dwelling.
Swiftly go forth, O great-minded, around, with your dear abode, where the gods say "thus."
Preparing the unprepared for the people, urging on strengths, flow the rain of heaven around.
This is he who, swift-moving from heaven, has flowed to the filter, the wave of the river.
Pressed, he goes to the filter, bearing brilliance with strength, seeing and illuminating.
Pressed, he serves from far and near; honey is poured for Indra.
They sing together, they urge the bay one with stones, the drop for Indra's drinking.
The cows urge the sun, the sisters their lord, great, the great drop, pleasing the great.
Flow, flowing one, with light after light, the god pressed for the gods; enter all treasures.
Flow, flowing one, fair praise, rain, service for the gods; flow for strength, in well-regulated fashion.
The wakeful guardian of the people has been born, Agni, the skilful, for the new well-being; with ghee-front, touching great heaven, he shines pure and splendid for the Bharatas.
O Agni, the Angirases found you hidden in the cave, lodged in forest after forest; you are born when churned; they call you great in strength, son of strength, Angiras.
The men kindle in the three-seated place Agni, the first household priest, banner of the sacrifice; he, sharing a chariot with Indra and the gods, sits on the grass, the skilful priest, to sacrifice.
This soma is pressed for you, Mitra and Varuna, strengtheners of truth; hear my call here.
Kings, not harming, in the firm highest seat, you two attain the thousand-pillared hall.
They, the two sovereigns, with ghee-pouring, Adityas, lords of the giver, go together unfailing.
Seeking the head of the horse that was hidden in the mountains, he found it in Sharyanavat.
This ancient praise of Indra and Agni for you was born of the thought, like rain from the cloud.
Hear the call of the singer, Indra and Agni; accept the songs; rule and nourish the thoughts.
Not for wickedness, O men, Indra and Agni; not for curse; do not give us to the reviler.
The bull, the seer, beloved in the nest, shines with the gods, the flowing, unconquerable one.
Set by thought, flowing, roaring toward the nest, he mounted Vayu by law.
I, O Soma, milking you by night and by day in the brown udder, would fly beyond the Sun that burns with heat, like birds.
The ruddy one has entered the nest; the bull has gone to the pressed Indra; let him sit in the firm seat.
Now bring us, O drop, great wealth from all sides; flow to us a thousandfold.
